title: On the Robustness of Interpretability Methods
venue: ICML 2018 Workshop on Human Interpretability in Machine Learning (WHI); arXiv:1806.08049
problem: Robustness (similar inputs should get similar explanations) is a key desideratum of interpretability but is not measured.
method: Local Lipschitz estimate of explanation change within an eps-ball (continuous optimisation; discrete sample-based version for categorical data); LIME, SHAP and gradient-based methods.
data: UCI datasets (e.g., Boston) and COMPAS with black-box classifiers; MNIST and ImageNet for gradient methods (p.3).
evaluation: Local Lipschitz estimates aggregated over test points.
findings: Current methods, including LIME and SHAP, performed poorly on the robustness metrics; very close points received considerably different explanations (abstract; Sec.3).
limitations: Authors: robustness may conflict with other goals; enforcing robustness proposed as future work (Sec.4). Ours: short workshop paper.

venue: ICML 2019 Workshop on AI for Social Good; arXiv:1904.12991

venue: AdvML '20: Workshop on Adversarial Learning Methods for Machine Learning and Data Mining (KDD 2020); arXiv:2006.12302

title: Reliable Post hoc Explanations: Modeling Uncertainty in Explainability
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34 (NeurIPS 2021)
problem: LIME and KernelSHAP explanations are inconsistent and unstable, give no measure of their reliability and need hyper-parameter tuning.
method: Bayesian versions of LIME and KernelSHAP that return credible intervals for feature importances; 'perturbations-to-go' estimate of the samples needed for a target certainty; focused sampling of perturbations.

title: S-LIME: Stabilized-LIME for Model Explanation
venue: Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining
event: KDD '21: The 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining

method: S-LIME: hypothesis tests based on a central limit theorem for LARS/LASSO variable-entry decisions decide adaptively how many perturbation samples LIME needs for a stable top-k feature set.

problem: Existing stability metrics consider only input change and ignore the model's internal representation and output.

title: Statistical stability indices for LIME: Obtaining reliable explanations for machine learning models
venue: Journal of the Operational Research Society
problem: LIME gives different explanations for the same instance across repeated calls; the paper proposes indices to detect this instability.
method: Derives the sampling distribution of LIME's weighted ridge coefficients and proposes two indices: Variables Stability Index (concordance of selected features) and Coefficients Stability Index (equality tests on coefficients) across repeated LIME calls.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Local Model Explanations Without Model Access
problem: When only a static sample of model inputs and outputs is available, local explanations carry finite-sample uncertainty that current explainers do not quantify.

problem: Local explanations near complex decision boundaries are brittle and their uncertainty is not quantified.
